key_insight: For the learning tasks studied, bound entanglement alone does not guarantee exponential quantum advantage; violating the reduction criterion appears necessary.
engineering_relevance: Designing quantum learning protocols should prioritize resource states and measurements that break the reduction criterion, since bound-entangled or restricted-correlations resources cannot sustain the strongest sample-complexity gains.
method: Analyze n-qubit Pauli-channel learning under the reduction criterion for both inputs and measurements.
Compare incoherent adaptive protocols with one-sided coherent adaptive protocols when one side is restricted.
Extend the argument to conjugate-state learning using conditional min-entropy to quantify how bounds change with larger criterion violations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports proof-based lower bounds showing that restricting either inputs or measurements to satisfy the reduction criterion removes exponential advantage, while an exponential lower bound still persists for the one-sided coherent case and restricted joint measurements fail in conjugate-state learning.
watch_item: These results are task-specific and theoretical, so applying them to practical hardware will require checking whether the relevant states and measurement schemes truly violate the reduction criterion under noise and finite-depth constraints.
paper_title: Bound Entanglement Is Insufficient for an Exponential Quantum Learning Advantage
